sectors.agriculture: Farming, viticulture, forestry, horticulture, fishing, and the first processing of what they produce.
sectors.construction: Building and civil works, and the trades on site: masonry, carpentry, roofing, plumbing, heating, electrical installation, painting, renovation.
sectors.manufacturing: Making physical goods: production, machining, assembly, workshop and industrial processing, food production.
sectors.energy-environment: Electricity, heating, water, waste, recycling, remediation, environmental services.
sectors.wholesale-trade: Buying and selling goods to businesses: import, export, distribution, trading, representation.
sectors.retail: Selling goods to the public, in a shop or online.
sectors.hospitality: Restaurants, cafés, bars, catering, hotels, guest accommodation, tourism.
sectors.transport-logistics: Carrying goods or people, freight forwarding, warehousing, delivery, removals, taxi and coach.
sectors.it-services: Software, IT services, hosting, networks, data, artificial intelligence, electronics and telecoms engineering.
sectors.engineering: Technical design offices: architecture, civil, mechanical and electrical engineering, surveying, laboratory and testing work.
sectors.marketing-media: Advertising, communication, graphic and web design, publishing, audiovisual production, events, public relations.
sectors.finance: Banking, credit, asset and fund management, insurance and its broking, payment and financial services.
sectors.holding: Acquisition, holding and management of participations in other companies, and management of the group's own assets. The purpose describes owning rather than operating.
sectors.real-estate: Owning, letting, managing, brokering or developing property.
sectors.legal-accounting: Law, notarial work, fiduciary and accounting services, audit, tax and payroll administration.
sectors.consulting: Advice and services to businesses that are none of the above: management, strategy, organisation, human resources, recruitment, training of staff, administrative support.
sectors.health-care: Medical, dental, veterinary and paramedical practice, therapy, care homes, home care, pharmacies, medical analysis.
sectors.education: Schools, teaching, vocational and language training, coaching, childcare.
sectors.personal-services: Services to individuals: hairdressing, beauty, wellbeing, cleaning, security, repair, funeral services, domestic work.
sectors.non-profit: An association, foundation or cooperative whose purpose is charitable, cultural, sporting, religious, professional or otherwise not for profit.
sectors.other: The purpose text does not place the company in any sector above, or describes something too general to place.

segments.sme-owner: A small owner-run business, typically under 50 people, where the owner decides.
segments.mature-sme: An established firm, long registered, with structured operations and likely several sites or departments.
segments.data-driven: Work that produces or depends on substantial data: analytics, laboratories, logistics, finance, research.
segments.ai-adopter: Purpose text mentions software, automation, digital products or AI as part of what the company does.
segments.compliance-sector: Regulated activity: health, finance, insurance, legal, public mandates, personal data at the centre.
segments.lean-startup: Recently registered, small capital, product or technology purpose rather than trade or services.
